hero.title: Acceptability of a Mixed Reality Tool to Support Pain and Anxiety During Minor Gynaecological Procedures
hero.subtitle: A research study exploring how mixed reality technology may support comfort, breathing, and anxiety management during outpatient gynaecological procedures.

about.title: About the Study
about.annaCaption: Hi, I am Anna. How are you?
about.overviewText: This study addresses the common issues of pain and anxiety experienced during outpatient gynecological procedures, such as intrauterine device (IUD) insertion, hysteroscopy, and colposcopy. While non-pharmacological interventions like breathing exercises and relaxation have been shown to be effective in managing stress and anxiety related to these procedures, they are not routinely offered due to limitations in clinical time and the specific skills required from clinicians. The core objective of this research is to evaluate the acceptability and feasibility of a newly developed mixed reality (MR) prototype. This system utilizes a virtual support character to guide patients through research-backed stress-management interventions such as breathing exercises or distraction techniques while allowing the patient to maintain interaction with their treating clinician in the physical environment.
goals: Evaluate usability and comfort of MR devices
Explore feasibility in a clinical setting
Investigate effectiveness of support strategies delivered by MR

devices.title: Devices Used
devices.intro: This study uses the following mixed reality and augmented reality devices.

items.name: Meta Quest 3
items.note: Great center of gravity and clear passthrough; however, remains front-heavy during long sessions.

items.name: Meta Quest 3S
items.note: Stable weight distribution; but bulkier with a narrower visual sweet spot.

items.name: XREAL One AR glasses
items.note: Ultra-light and non-intrusive; but offers a limited field of view and requires a wired connection.
